"""
    ThermalMPOGap.CertifiedMPO.Norms

Rigorous operator and Hilbert--Schmidt norm witnesses for exact rational MPOs: local maps,
gauges, interval Cholesky acceptance, squared-tail bounds, and the sparse exact core encoding.
Moved verbatim from spin2 `Spin2MPONorms`; `encode_fraction`/`parse_fraction` are the
`ExactArithmetic` ones (identical code), re-bound here so `Norms.encode_fraction` still works.
"""
module Norms

using LinearAlgebra
import Nemo
using ..CertifiedMPO: F, nemo_array, encode_fraction, parse_fraction

"Numerical candidate generation with a QR fallback for a failed divide-and-conquer SVD."
function numerical_svd(A; full = false)
    @assert all(isfinite, A)
    try
        return svd(A; full)
    catch err
        err isa LinearAlgebra.LAPACKException || rethrow()
        return svd(A; alg = LinearAlgebra.QRIteration(), full)
    end
end

"Dyadic upper square root, accepted by an integer square comparison."
function upper_sqrt(x::F; bits = 80)
    @assert x >= 0 && bits >= 0
    denominator = big(2)^bits
    square = cld(numerator(x)*denominator^2, Base.denominator(x))
    root = isqrt(square)
    root^2 < square && (root += 1)
    result = root//denominator
    @assert result^2 >= x
    return result
end

"Scale before taking a dyadic upper square root, preserving relative accuracy for tiny residuals."
function relative_upper_sqrt(x::F; bits = 80)
    @assert x >= 0
    iszero(x) && return F(0)
    exponent = fld(ndigits(numerator(x); base = 2)-ndigits(denominator(x); base = 2), 2)
    scale = exponent >= 0 ? F(big(2)^exponent) : F(1, big(2)^(-exponent))
    return scale*upper_sqrt(x/scale^2; bits)
end

"Round a nonnegative rational upward to a dyadic with bounded relative precision."
function relative_rational_upper(x::F; bits = 128)
    @assert x >= 0 && bits >= 1
    iszero(x) && return F(0)
    exponent = ndigits(numerator(x); base = 2)-ndigits(denominator(x); base = 2)-bits
    scale = exponent >= 0 ? F(big(2)^exponent) : F(1, big(2)^(-exponent))
    scaled = x/scale
    result = cld(numerator(scaled), denominator(scaled))*scale
    @assert x <= result < x+scale
    return result
end

"Quantize a real MPO candidate; this defines its exact rational coefficients."
function quantize(cores; bits = 48)
    denominator = big(2)^bits
    @assert all(all(isreal, core) for core in cores)
    return [[round(BigInt, real(x)*denominator)//denominator for x in core] for core in cores]
end

"Bound one partial-operator family through a core (left, output, input, right)."
function propagate(core::Array{F,4}, previous; bits = 80)
    l, dout, din, r = size(core)
    @assert l == length(previous) && all(>=(0), previous)
    result = zeros(F, r)
    for a in 1:r
        envelope = zeros(F, dout, din)
        for s in 1:dout, t in 1:din, b in 1:l
            envelope[s, t] += abs(core[b, s, t, a])*previous[b]
        end
        # If ||X_st|| <= C_st, then ||[X_st]|| <= ||C||_2.
        one_norm = maximum(sum(envelope; dims = 1))
        infinity_norm = maximum(sum(envelope; dims = 2))
        result[a] = upper_sqrt(one_norm*infinity_norm; bits)
    end
    return result
end

"Rigorous operator-norm witnesses from both directions and every MPO cut."
function witness(cores; bits = 80)
    @assert !isempty(cores) && size(first(cores), 1) == size(last(cores), 4) == 1
    @assert all(size(cores[j], 4) == size(cores[j+1], 1) for j in 1:(length(cores)-1))
    left = Vector{F}[F[1]]
    for core in cores
        push!(left, propagate(core, last(left); bits))
    end
    right = [F[] for _ in 1:(length(cores)+1)]
    right[end] = F[1]
    for j in length(cores):-1:1
        right[j] = propagate(permutedims(cores[j], (4, 2, 3, 1)), right[j+1]; bits)
    end
    cuts = [sum(left[j] .* right[j]) for j in eachindex(left)]
    return (; upper = minimum(cuts), cuts, left, right)
end

"View a core as an operator from (left,input) to (right,output)."
function local_operator(core)
    l, dout, din, r = size(core)
    return reshape(permutedims(core, (2, 4, 3, 1)), dout*r, din*l)
end

"Contract two adjacent cores exactly, preserving their physical operator."
function merge_cores(first, second; field = Nemo.QQ)
    l, do1, di1, mid = size(first)
    @assert size(second, 1) == mid
    _, do2, di2, r = size(second)
    A = Nemo.matrix(field, reshape(first, l*do1*di1, mid))
    B = Nemo.matrix(field, reshape(second, mid, do2*di2*r))
    product = A*B
    raw = reshape(nemo_array(product, field), l, do1, di1, do2, di2, r)
    return reshape(permutedims(raw, (1, 4, 2, 5, 3, 6)), l, do1*do2, di1*di2, r)
end

"Exact positive rational gauges, proposed by a numerical logarithmic search."
function rational_gauges(cores, x; bits = 40)
    @assert all(isfinite, x) && bits >= 0
    dimensions = [size(c, 4) for c in cores[1:(end-1)]]
    @assert length(x) == sum(dimensions)
    denominator = big(2)^bits
    result = Vector{F}[F[1]]
    offset = 0
    for d in dimensions
        z = x[(offset+1):(offset+d)]
        # A common factor on one bond cancels in the product of local norms.
        weights = exp.(z .- maximum(z))
        push!(result, [max(big(1), round(BigInt, w*denominator))//denominator for w in weights])
        offset += d
    end
    push!(result, F[1])
    return result
end

"Apply rational vector/diagonal or full-matrix gauges with exact cancellation."
function gauge_transform(cores, gauges; interval_precision = nothing)
    @assert length(gauges) == length(cores)+1
    if first(gauges) isa AbstractMatrix
        @assert all(g -> g isa AbstractMatrix, gauges)
        @assert first(gauges) == last(gauges) == ones(F, 1, 1)
        matrices = [Nemo.matrix(Nemo.QQ, g) for g in gauges]
        inverses = inv.(matrices)
        for (g, inverse) in zip(matrices, inverses)
            @assert g*inverse == Nemo.identity_matrix(Nemo.QQ, Nemo.nrows(g))
        end
        RR = isnothing(interval_precision) ? nothing : Nemo.ArbField(interval_precision)
        interval_matrices = isnothing(RR) ? nothing : [Nemo.matrix(RR, g) for g in gauges]
        interval_inverses =
            isnothing(RR) ? nothing : [Nemo.matrix(RR, nemo_array(g)) for g in inverses]
        result = isnothing(RR) ? Array{F,4}[] : Any[]
        for (j, core) in enumerate(cores)
            l, d, di, r = size(core)
            @assert size(gauges[j]) == (l, l) && size(gauges[j+1]) == (r, r)
            # The terminal core remains exact for the final bridge equality.
            # Elsewhere only an enclosure is needed for residual/norm checks.
            field = isnothing(RR) || j == length(cores) ? Nemo.QQ : RR
            g = field === Nemo.QQ ? matrices[j] : interval_matrices[j]
            inverse = field === Nemo.QQ ? inverses[j+1] : interval_inverses[j+1]
            left = g*Nemo.matrix(field, reshape(core, l, d*di*r))
            right = Nemo.matrix(field, reshape(nemo_array(left, field), l*d*di, r))*inverse
            push!(result, reshape(nemo_array(right, field), l, d, di, r))
        end
        return result
    end
    @assert all(g -> g isa AbstractVector, gauges)
    @assert first(gauges) == last(gauges) == F[1]
    @assert all(all(>(0), g) for g in gauges)
    result = Array{F,4}[]
    for (j, core) in enumerate(cores)
        l, dout, din, r = size(core)
        @assert length(gauges[j]) == l && length(gauges[j+1]) == r
        push!(
            result,
            [
                core[b, s, t, a]*gauges[j][b]/gauges[j+1][a] for
                b in 1:l, s in 1:dout, t in 1:din, a in 1:r
            ],
        )
    end
    return result
end

"One exact transformed core for an inconclusive interval-residual fallback."
function exact_gauge_core(core, left_gauge, right_gauge)
    l, d, di, r = size(core)
    if left_gauge isa AbstractVector
        @assert length(left_gauge) == l && length(right_gauge) == r
        return core .* reshape(left_gauge, l, 1, 1, 1) ./ reshape(right_gauge, 1, 1, 1, r)
    end
    @assert size(left_gauge) == (l, l) && size(right_gauge) == (r, r)
    left_matrix, right_matrix = Nemo.matrix(Nemo.QQ, left_gauge), Nemo.matrix(Nemo.QQ, right_gauge)
    inverse = inv(right_matrix)
    @assert right_matrix*inverse == Nemo.identity_matrix(Nemo.QQ, r)
    left = left_matrix*Nemo.matrix(Nemo.QQ, reshape(core, l, d*di*r))
    right = Nemo.matrix(Nemo.QQ, reshape(nemo_array(left), l*d*di, r))*inverse
    return reshape(nemo_array(right), l, d, di, r)
end

"Portable gauges, retaining the original vector encoding for diagonal witnesses."
encode_gauges(gauges) = [
    g isa AbstractMatrix ?
    Dict("dimensions"=>collect(size(g)), "entries"=>encode_fraction.(vec(g))) :
    encode_fraction.(g) for g in gauges
]

decode_gauges(encoded) = [
    g isa AbstractVector ? parse_fraction.(g) :
    reshape(parse_fraction.(g["entries"]), Int.(g["dimensions"])...) for g in encoded
]

"Build an outward-rounded Gram matrix in the smaller local space."
function local_gram(W::AbstractMatrix; precision = 192)
    RR = Nemo.ArbField(precision)
    M = Nemo.matrix(RR, W)
    return size(W, 1) <= size(W, 2) ? M*transpose(M) : transpose(M)*M
end

"Accept a local spectral norm upper bound only after rigorous Arb Cholesky."
function verify_gram_bound(gram, alpha::F; metric = nothing)
    alpha > 0 || return false
    RR = Nemo.base_ring(gram)
    C = -gram
    for i in 1:Nemo.nrows(C)
        C[i, i] += RR(alpha)^2*(isnothing(metric) ? RR(1) : RR(metric[i]))
    end
    try
        Nemo.cholesky(C)
        return true
    catch err
        # arb_mat_cho returns failure if positive definiteness is not certain.
        if err isa ErrorException && err.msg == "Matrix is not positive definite"
            return false
        end
        rethrow()
    end
end

"Rational weighted Gram pair for the norm from column metric to row metric."
function weighted_gram(W; row_metric = nothing, col_metric = nothing, precision = 192)
    if isnothing(row_metric) && isnothing(col_metric)
        return local_gram(W; precision), nothing
    end
    rows = isnothing(row_metric) ? ones(F, size(W, 1)) : F.(row_metric)
    cols = isnothing(col_metric) ? ones(F, size(W, 2)) : F.(col_metric)
    @assert length(rows) == size(W, 1) && length(cols) == size(W, 2)
    @assert all(>(0), rows) && all(>(0), cols)
    RR = Nemo.ArbField(precision)
    M = Nemo.matrix(RR, W)
    scaled = deepcopy(M)
    if size(W, 1) <= size(W, 2)
        for j in eachindex(cols), i in eachindex(rows)
            scaled[i, j] /= RR(cols[j])
        end
        return scaled*transpose(M), inv.(rows)
    end
    for j in eachindex(cols), i in eachindex(rows)
        scaled[i, j] *= RR(rows[i])
    end
    return transpose(M)*scaled, cols
end

function verify_local_bound(
    W::AbstractMatrix,
    alpha::F;
    precision = 192,
    row_metric = nothing,
    col_metric = nothing,
)
    alpha == 0 && return all(iszero, W)
    alpha < 0 && return false
    gram, metric = weighted_gram(W; precision, row_metric, col_metric)
    return verify_gram_bound(gram, alpha; metric)
end

"Numerical proposals are independently accepted or rejected by ball arithmetic."
function local_norm_upper(
    W::AbstractMatrix;
    precision = 192,
    bits = 48,
    row_metric = nothing,
    col_metric = nothing,
)
    all(iszero, W) && return F(0)
    candidate = Float64.(W)
    if !isnothing(row_metric)
        candidate .*= sqrt.(Float64.(row_metric))
    end
    if !isnothing(col_metric)
        candidate ./= transpose(sqrt.(Float64.(col_metric)))
    end
    estimate = try
        opnorm(candidate)
    catch err
        err isa LinearAlgebra.LAPACKException || rethrow()
        first(svd(candidate; alg = LinearAlgebra.QRIteration()).S)
    end
    @assert isfinite(estimate) && estimate > 0 && bits >= 0
    gram, metric = weighted_gram(W; precision, row_metric, col_metric)
    denominator = big(2)^bits
    exponent = last(frexp(estimate))-1
    scale = exponent >= 0 ? F(big(2)^exponent) : F(1, big(2)^(-exponent))
    for attempt in 0:12
        proposal = estimate*(1+10.0^(attempt-10))
        alpha = scale*((ceil(BigInt, (proposal/Float64(scale))*denominator)+1)//denominator)
        verify_gram_bound(gram, alpha; metric) && return alpha
    end
    error("No local norm bound passed the interval Cholesky check")
end

"Physical Hilbert--Schmidt row metric, in (left,output,input) order."
function hs_row_metric(left, d, weights)
    isnothing(weights) && return ones(F, left*d*d)
    @assert length(weights) == d && all(>(0), weights)
    return vec([F(weights[t])/F(weights[s]) for b in 1:left, s in 1:d, t in 1:d])
end

"A local rational map and its physical input/output metrics."
function core_map(core, kind, weights = nothing)
    l, d, di, r = size(core)
    @assert d == di
    @assert isnothing(weights) || (length(weights)==d && all(>(0), weights))
    if kind == :operator
        W = local_operator(core)
        rows = isnothing(weights) ? nothing : repeat(inv.(F.(weights)), r)
        cols = isnothing(weights) ? nothing : repeat(inv.(F.(weights)), l)
    elseif kind == :left_hs
        W = left_hs_map(core)
        rows = isnothing(weights) ? nothing : hs_row_metric(l, d, weights)
        cols = nothing
    elseif kind == :right_hs
        W = right_hs_map(core)
        rows = isnothing(weights) ? nothing : repeat(hs_row_metric(1, d, weights), r)
        cols = nothing
    else
        error("Unknown local map kind")
    end
    return W, rows, cols
end

"Physical adjoint in the rational polynomial basis; virtual order is unchanged."
function adjoint_cores(cores; weights = nothing)
    return [
        [
            (isnothing(weights) ? F(1) : F(weights[s])/F(weights[t]))*c[b, t, s, a] for
            b in axes(c, 1), s in axes(c, 3), t in axes(c, 2), a in axes(c, 4)
        ] for c in cores
    ]
end

"Exact spatial reflection. This is unitary on the full physical Hilbert space."
reflect_cores(cores) = [permutedims(c, (4, 2, 3, 1)) for c in reverse(cores)]

function core_norm_upper(core, kind; weights = nothing, kwargs...)
    W, rows, cols = core_map(core, kind, weights)
    return local_norm_upper(W; row_metric = rows, col_metric = cols, kwargs...)
end

function verify_core_bound(core, kind, alpha; weights = nothing, kwargs...)
    W, rows, cols = core_map(core, kind, weights)
    return verify_local_bound(W, alpha; row_metric = rows, col_metric = cols, kwargs...)
end

"Global MPO norm bound from a sequence of rigorously bounded local maps."
function local_product_witness(cores, gauges; precision = 192, bits = 48, weights = nothing)
    transformed = gauge_transform(cores, gauges)
    bounds = [core_norm_upper(c, :operator; precision, bits, weights) for c in transformed]
    return (; upper = prod(bounds), bounds)
end

"Independent replay of proposed local bounds, without an SVD or optimizer."
function verify_local_product(
    cores,
    gauges,
    bounds;
    precision = 192,
    weights = nothing,
    interval_precision = nothing,
)
    length(bounds) == length(cores) || return false
    transformed = gauge_transform(cores, gauges; interval_precision)
    return all(
        verify_core_bound(c, :operator, alpha; precision, weights) for
        (c, alpha) in zip(transformed, bounds)
    )
end

"Sparse exact core encoding, independent of floating-point JSON semantics."
function encode_cores(cores)
    return [
        Dict(
            "dimensions"=>collect(size(c)),
            "entries"=>[[i, encode_fraction(c[i])] for i in eachindex(c) if !iszero(c[i])],
        ) for c in cores
    ]
end

function decode_cores(encoded)
    result = Array{F,4}[]
    for row in encoded
        dimensions = Int.(row["dimensions"])
        @assert length(dimensions) == 4 && all(>(0), dimensions)
        c = zeros(F, dimensions...)
        seen = Set{Int}()
        for pair in row["entries"]
            i = Int(pair[1])
            @assert 1 <= i <= length(c) && !(i in seen)
            push!(seen, i)
            c[i] = parse_fraction(pair[2])
        end
        push!(result, c)
    end
    return result
end

"A right-tail coefficient map to Hilbert--Schmidt operators."
function right_hs_map(core)
    l, dout, din, r = size(core)
    return reshape(permutedims(core, (2, 3, 4, 1)), dout*din*r, l)
end

"A left-prefix coefficient map to Hilbert--Schmidt operators."
left_hs_map(core) = reshape(core, prod(size(core)[1:3]), size(core, 4))

"Bounds on the coefficient maps of all squared MPO tails, without a four-layer contraction."
function squared_tail_witness(
    cores;
    gauges = nothing,
    precision = 192,
    cap_frobenius = true,
    blocksize = 1,
    weights = nothing,
    adjoint_first = false,
    return_operator_cores = false,
    arithmetic = :rational,
)
    @assert blocksize in (1, 2)
    @assert arithmetic in (:rational, :interval)
    first_copy = adjoint_first ? adjoint_cores(cores; weights) : cores
    operator_cores =
        isnothing(gauges) ? first_copy :
        gauge_transform(
            first_copy,
            gauges;
            interval_precision = arithmetic == :interval ? precision : nothing,
        )
    local_operator_bounds =
        [core_norm_upper(c, :operator; weights, precision) for c in operator_cores]
    local_hs_bounds = [core_norm_upper(c, :right_hs; weights, precision) for c in cores]
    block_bounds =
        blocksize == 2 ?
        [
            core_norm_upper(
                merge_cores(
                    operator_cores[j],
                    operator_cores[j+1];
                    field = arithmetic == :interval ? Nemo.ArbField(precision) : Nemo.QQ,
                ),
                :operator;
                weights = isnothing(weights) ? nothing : kron(weights, weights),
                precision,
            ) for j in 1:(length(cores)-1)
        ] : F[]
    operator_tail = ones(F, length(cores)+1)
    hs_tail = ones(F, length(cores)+1)
    for j in length(cores):-1:1
        operator_tail[j] = operator_tail[j+1]*local_operator_bounds[j]
        if blocksize == 2 && j < length(cores)
            operator_tail[j] = min(operator_tail[j], block_bounds[j]*operator_tail[j+2])
        end
        hs_tail[j] = hs_tail[j+1]*local_hs_bounds[j]
        if cap_frobenius
            # The first-copy tails are g_a R_a. The HS coefficient-map
            # bound gives sum_a ||g_a R_a||_F^2 <= gamma^2 sum_a g_a^2.
            weight2 = isnothing(gauges) ? F(size(cores[j], 1)) : sum(abs2, gauges[j])
            operator_tail[j] = min(operator_tail[j], hs_tail[j]*relative_upper_sqrt(weight2))
        end
    end
    # For R(v)=sum_a v_a R_a and K(V)=sum_ab V_ab R_a R_b,
    # K(V)=[R_1 ... R_D] col_a(sum_b V_ab R_b).
    # Therefore ||K||_(F <- F) <= ||[R_1 ... R_D]||_op ||R||_(F <- 2).
    certificate = (;
        upper = operator_tail .* hs_tail,
        operator_tail,
        hs_tail,
        local_operator_bounds,
        local_hs_bounds,
        frobenius_capped = cap_frobenius,
        block_bounds,
    )
    return return_operator_cores ? (; certificate, operator_cores) : certificate
end

end

"""
    ThermalMPOGap.ExactArithmetic

Exact rational arithmetic with outward rounding. Every routine returns rationals, and every
enclosure is valid without floating point, so its output can certify an inequality.

Moved verbatim from spin1 (`optimize_bounds.jl`, `temperature_lift.jl`) and spin2
(`Spin2MPONorms.jl`); only the rounding scale became an explicit argument.
"""
module ExactArithmetic

export RationalBig, frac, round_up, round_down, log_enclosure, first_true, integer_root,
    power_interval, power_upper, encode_fraction, parse_fraction, parse_rational

"Exact rationals with arbitrary-precision numerator and denominator."
const RationalBig = Rational{BigInt}

"The rational a/b with `BigInt` numerator and denominator."
frac(a::Integer, b::Integer = 1) = BigInt(a) // BigInt(b)

"Smallest point of the grid (1/scale)ℤ that is ≥ x."
round_up(x, scale) = frac(cld(numerator(x) * scale, denominator(x)), scale)

"Largest point of the grid (1/scale)ℤ that is ≤ x."
round_down(x, scale) = frac(fld(numerator(x) * scale, denominator(x)), scale)

"""
    log_enclosure(x) -> (lower, upper)

Outward rational enclosure of log x for rational x ≥ 1, by range reduction to [1, 2) and the
atanh series with its remainder. Both ends lie on the grid 10⁻²⁴.
"""
function log_enclosure(x::RationalBig)
    @assert x >= 1
    k = ndigits(numerator(x); base = 2) - ndigits(denominator(x); base = 2)
    k = max(k, 0)
    while frac(2)^k > x
        k -= 1
    end
    while frac(2)^(k + 1) <= x
        k += 1
    end
    y = x / frac(2)^k
    @assert 1 <= y < 2
    function series(z)
        @assert 0 <= z <= frac(1, 3)
        terms = 40
        partial = 2sum(z^(2j + 1) / (2j + 1) for j in 0:(terms-1))
        remainder = 2z^(2terms + 1) / ((2terms + 1) * (1 - z^2))
        return partial, partial + remainder
    end
    # Rounding the mantissa first keeps the rational powers small.
    grid = big(10)^24
    yl, yu = round_down(y, grid), round_up(y, grid)
    lower, _ = series((yl - 1) / (yl + 1))
    _, upper = series((yu - 1) / (yu + 1))
    l2, u2 = series(frac(1, 3))
    return round_down(k * l2 + lower, grid), round_up(k * u2 + upper, grid)
end

"""
    first_true(predicate, lo, hi; digits = 12) -> (a, b)

Bisection on the decimal grid 10^-digits for an increasing predicate: returns adjacent grid
points with `predicate(a) == false` and `predicate(b) == true`.
"""
function first_true(predicate, lo, hi; digits = 12)
    scale = big(10)^digits
    a, b = fld(numerator(lo) * scale, denominator(lo)), cld(numerator(hi) * scale, denominator(hi))
    @assert !predicate(frac(a, scale)) && predicate(frac(b, scale))
    while b - a > 1
        middle = fld(a + b, 2)
        if predicate(frac(middle, scale))
            b = middle
        else
            a = middle
        end
    end
    @assert !predicate(frac(a, scale)) && predicate(frac(b, scale))
    return frac(a, scale), frac(b, scale)
end

"Floor of the positive integer bth root, without floating-point arithmetic."
function integer_root(n::BigInt, b::Int)
    @assert n >= 0 && b >= 1
    b == 1 && return n
    b == 2 && return isqrt(n)
    n == 0 && return big(0)
    lo = big(0)
    hi = big(1) << cld(ndigits(n; base = 2), b)
    while hi - lo > 1
        mid = (lo + hi) >> 1
        if mid^b <= n
            lo = mid
        else
            hi = mid
        end
    end
    @assert lo^b <= n < (lo + 1)^b
    return lo
end

"Outward enclosure of x^r for nonnegative rational x and r, on the grid 10^-digits."
function power_interval(x::RationalBig, r::RationalBig; digits = 24)
    @assert x >= 0 && r >= 0
    r == 0 && return (frac(1), frac(1))
    x == 0 && return (frac(0), frac(0))
    a, b = Int(numerator(r)), Int(denominator(r))
    b == 1 && return (x^a, x^a)
    scale = big(10)^digits
    target = x^a
    n = fld(numerator(target) * scale^b, denominator(target))
    root = integer_root(n, b)
    lo = frac(root, scale)
    hi = lo^b == target ? lo : frac(root + 1, scale)
    @assert lo^b <= target <= hi^b
    return lo, hi
end

"Upper end of `power_interval`."
power_upper(x, r) = last(power_interval(x, r))

"""
    encode_fraction(x) -> String

Exact token for a rational: `"num//den"`, or `"num//2^k"` when the denominator is a power of
two and the exponent form is shorter.
"""
function encode_fraction(x::Rational)
    den = denominator(x)
    if ispow2(den)
        exponent = ndigits(den; base = 2) - 1
        token = "2^" * string(exponent)
        if length(token) < ndigits(den)
            return string(numerator(x)) * "//" * token
        end
    end
    return string(x)
end

"Inverse of `encode_fraction`; requires the `num//den` or `num//2^k` form."
function parse_fraction(s)
    parts = split(s, "//")
    @assert length(parts) == 2
    den = if startswith(parts[2], "2^")
        exponent = parse(Int, parts[2][3:end])
        @assert exponent >= 0
        big(1) << exponent
    else
        parse(BigInt, parts[2])
    end
    @assert !iszero(den)
    return parse(BigInt, parts[1]) // den
end

"""
    parse_rational(x)

Exact rational from an integer, an integer string, `"a/b"`, `"a//b"`, or a dictionary with
`numerator` and `denominator`. Refuses floating-point input.
"""
parse_rational(x::Integer) = frac(x)
parse_rational(x::AbstractDict) =
    frac(_integer(x["numerator"]), _integer(x["denominator"]))
function parse_rational(x::AbstractString)
    parts = split(x, r"/+")
    return length(parts) == 1 ? frac(_integer(parts[1])) :
           frac(_integer(parts[1]), _integer(parts[2]))
end
parse_rational(x) = error("Refusing inexact rational input: $(typeof(x))")

_integer(x::AbstractString) = parse(BigInt, x)
_integer(x::Integer) = BigInt(x)
_integer(x) = error("Refusing inexact integer input: $(typeof(x))")

end

"""
    ThermalMPOGap.CertifiedMPO.Products

Certified zip-up compression of an MPO product A·B with unequal auxiliary dimensions (in
rational or interval candidate arithmetic), its replay, its witness encoding, and the
three-layer overlap ⟨C, A·B⟩ in Arb. Moved verbatim from spin2 `Spin2MPOProducts`; `MS` is
`CertifiedMPO.Squaring` instead of a private include copy.
"""
module Products

using LinearAlgebra
import Nemo
using ..CertifiedMPO: nemo_array
import ..Squaring
const MS=Squaring
const MN=MS.MN
const F=MN.F

"Three-layer overlap <C,A*B>, without constructing product cores or a full operator."
function product_inner_ball(C, A, B; weights = nothing, precision = 192)
    @assert length(C)==length(A)==length(B) && !isempty(C)
    RR=Nemo.ArbField(precision)
    environment=reshape([RR(1)], 1, 1, 1)
    for (c, a, b) in zip(C, A, B)
        lc, d, di, rc=size(c)
        la, da, mid, ra=size(a)
        lb, midb, dib, rb=size(b)
        @assert d==da && di==dib && mid==midb && size(environment)==(lc, la, lb)
        blocks(X) = [
            any(!iszero, X[:, s, t, :]) ? Nemo.matrix(RR, X[:, s, t, :]) : nothing for
            s in axes(X, 2), t in axes(X, 3)
        ]
        cb, ab, bb=blocks(c), blocks(a), blocks(b)
        incoming=Nemo.matrix(RR, reshape(permutedims(environment, (1, 3, 2)), lc*lb, la))
        outgoing=Nemo.zero_matrix(RR, rc*ra, rb)
        for s in 1:d, u in 1:mid
            isnothing(ab[s, u]) && continue
            contracted=incoming*ab[s, u]
            first=Nemo.matrix(RR, reshape(nemo_array(contracted, RR), lc, lb*ra))
            for t in 1:di
                (isnothing(cb[s, t]) || isnothing(bb[u, t])) && continue
                second=transpose(cb[s, t])*first
                raw=reshape(nemo_array(second, RR), rc, lb, ra)
                third=Nemo.matrix(RR, reshape(permutedims(raw, (1, 3, 2)), rc*ra, lb))*bb[u, t]
                weight=isnothing(weights) ? F(1) : F(weights[t])/F(weights[s])
                outgoing+=RR(weight)*third
            end
        end
        environment=reshape(nemo_array(outgoing, RR), rc, ra, rb)
    end
    @assert size(environment)==(1, 1, 1)
    return only(environment)
end

"Certified zip-up compression of A*B, including unequal auxiliary dimensions."
function product_candidate(
    A,
    B;
    maxdim = 16,
    bits = 48,
    precision = 192,
    weights = nothing,
    first_gauges = nothing,
    candidate_arithmetic = :rational,
    physical_charges = nothing,
    progress = nothing,
)
    @assert length(A)==length(B) && !isempty(A)
    @assert size(A[1], 1)==size(B[1], 1)==size(A[end], 4)==size(B[end], 4)==1
    @assert candidate_arithmetic in (:rational, :interval)
    RR = Nemo.ArbField(precision)
    first=isnothing(first_gauges) ? A :
          MN.gauge_transform(
        A,
        first_gauges;
        interval_precision = candidate_arithmetic == :interval ? precision : nothing,
    )
    charge_a = isnothing(physical_charges) ? nothing : MS.CB.infer_charges(first, physical_charges)
    charge_b = isnothing(physical_charges) ? nothing : MS.CB.infer_charges(B, physical_charges)
    prefix_charges = [0]
    operator_bounds=[MN.core_norm_upper(c, :operator; weights, precision) for c in first]
    hs_bounds=[MN.core_norm_upper(c, :right_hs; weights, precision) for c in B]
    n=length(A)
    tails=ones(F, n+1)
    for j in n:-1:1
        tails[j]=tails[j+1]*operator_bounds[j]*hs_bounds[j]
    end
    bridge=ones(F, 1, 1, 1)
    cores=Array{F,4}[]
    bridges=Array{F,3}[]
    residual_bounds, prefix_bounds=F[], F[]
    error, prefix=F(0), F(1)
    for j in 1:n
        # Interior products may use outward-rounded enclosures. The terminal
        # equality remains rational, closing the exact telescoping identity.
        field = candidate_arithmetic == :interval && j < n ? RR : Nemo.QQ
        Z =
            isnothing(physical_charges) ? MS.product_bridge(bridge, first[j], B[j]; field) :
            MS.CB.product_bridge(
                bridge,
                first[j],
                B[j],
                prefix_charges,
                charge_a[j],
                charge_a[j+1],
                charge_b[j],
                charge_b[j+1],
                physical_charges;
                field,
            )
        chi, d, di, ra, rb=size(Z)
        @assert d==di
        M=reshape(Z, chi*d*d, ra*rb)
        if j==n
            push!(cores, reshape(M, chi, d, d, 1))
            isnothing(progress) || progress((; stage = :compression, site = j, total = n))
            break
        end
        metric=MN.hs_row_metric(chi, d, weights)
        root=sqrt.(Float64.(metric))
        labels =
            isnothing(physical_charges) ? nothing :
            MS.CB.product_labels(prefix_charges, charge_a[j+1], charge_b[j+1], physical_charges)
        decomposition =
            isnothing(labels) ? MN.numerical_svd(Float64.(M) .* root) :
            MS.CB.truncated_svd(
                Float64.(M) .* root,
                labels...;
                maxdim,
                svd_function = MN.numerical_svd,
            )
        isnothing(labels) || (prefix_charges = decomposition.charges)
        rank=min(maxdim, length(decomposition.S))
        U=MS.relative_quantize(decomposition.U[:, 1:rank] ./ root; bits)
        R=MS.relative_quantize(Diagonal(decomposition.S[1:rank])*decomposition.Vt[1:rank, :]; bits)
        residual=M-MS.matrix_product(U, R, field)
        delta=MS.frobenius_upper(residual, field; metric)
        C=reshape(U, chi, d, d, rank)
        alpha=MN.core_norm_upper(C, :left_hs; weights, precision)
        error+=prefix*delta*tails[j+1]
        prefix*=alpha
        bridge=reshape(R, rank, ra, rb)
        push!(cores, C)
        push!(bridges, bridge)
        push!(residual_bounds, delta)
        push!(prefix_bounds, alpha)
        isnothing(progress) || progress((; stage = :compression, site = j, total = n))
    end
    return (;
        cores,
        bridges,
        residual_bounds,
        prefix_bounds,
        operator_bounds,
        hs_bounds,
        error,
        weights,
        first_gauges,
    )
end

"Replay the local product identities and all norm inequalities, without an SVD."
function verify_product(
    A,
    B,
    proof;
    precision = 192,
    residual_arithmetic = :rational,
    progress = nothing,
)
    @assert residual_arithmetic in (:rational, :interval)
    RR = Nemo.ArbField(precision)
    n=length(A)
    @assert length(B)==length(proof.cores)==length(proof.operator_bounds)==length(proof.hs_bounds)==n
    @assert length(proof.bridges)==length(proof.residual_bounds)==length(proof.prefix_bounds)==n-1
    weights=proof.weights
    first=isnothing(proof.first_gauges) ? A :
          MN.gauge_transform(
        A,
        proof.first_gauges;
        interval_precision = residual_arithmetic == :interval ? precision : nothing,
    )
    tails=ones(F, n+1)
    for j in n:-1:1
        @assert MN.verify_core_bound(
            first[j],
            :operator,
            proof.operator_bounds[j];
            weights,
            precision,
        )
        @assert MN.verify_core_bound(B[j], :right_hs, proof.hs_bounds[j]; weights, precision)
        tails[j]=tails[j+1]*proof.operator_bounds[j]*proof.hs_bounds[j]
    end
    bridge=ones(F, 1, 1, 1)
    prefix, error=F(1), F(0)
    for j in 1:n
        field = residual_arithmetic == :interval && j < n ? RR : Nemo.QQ
        Z=MS.product_bridge(bridge, first[j], B[j]; field)
        chi, d, di, ra, rb=size(Z)
        @assert d==di
        M=reshape(Z, chi*d*d, ra*rb)
        C=proof.cores[j]
        @assert size(C)[1:3]==(chi, d, d)
        if j==n
            @assert ra==rb==size(C, 4)==1 && reshape(C, size(M))==M
            isnothing(progress) || progress((; stage = :residuals, site = j, total = n))
            break
        end
        rank=size(C, 4)
        next=proof.bridges[j]
        @assert size(next)==(rank, ra, rb)
        U, R = reshape(C, chi*d*d, rank), reshape(next, rank, ra*rb)
        residual=M-MS.matrix_product(U, R, field)
        metric=MN.hs_row_metric(chi, d, weights)
        delta, alpha=proof.residual_bounds[j], proof.prefix_bounds[j]
        @assert delta >= 0
        if field === Nemo.QQ
            @assert delta^2 >= sum(abs2.(residual) .* metric)
        elseif !(RR(delta)^2 > sum(abs2.(residual) .* RR.(metric)))
            # Inconclusive intervals, including an exactly zero residual,
            # require the rational identity; they are never accepted directly.
            exact_core =
                isnothing(proof.first_gauges) ? A[j] :
                MN.exact_gauge_core(A[j], proof.first_gauges[j], proof.first_gauges[j+1])
            exact = reshape(MS.product_bridge(bridge, exact_core, B[j]), size(M))
            exact_residual = exact-MS.rational_product(U, R)
            @assert delta^2 >= sum(abs2.(exact_residual) .* metric)
        end
        @assert MN.verify_core_bound(C, :left_hs, alpha; weights, precision)
        error+=prefix*delta*tails[j+1]
        prefix*=alpha
        bridge=next
        isnothing(progress) || progress((; stage = :residuals, site = j, total = n))
    end
    @assert error==proof.error
    return true
end

function encode(A, B, proof)
    return Dict(
        "first_input"=>MN.encode_cores(A),
        "second_input"=>MN.encode_cores(B),
        "output"=>MN.encode_cores(proof.cores),
        "bridges"=>[
            Dict("dimensions"=>collect(size(R)), "entries"=>string.(vec(R))) for R in proof.bridges
        ],
        "residual_bounds"=>string.(proof.residual_bounds),
        "prefix_bounds"=>string.(proof.prefix_bounds),
        "operator_bounds"=>string.(proof.operator_bounds),
        "hs_bounds"=>string.(proof.hs_bounds),
        "weights"=>isnothing(proof.weights) ? nothing : string.(proof.weights),
        "first_gauges"=>isnothing(proof.first_gauges) ? nothing :
                        MN.encode_gauges(proof.first_gauges),
        "error"=>string(proof.error),
    )
end

function decode(data)
    A, B=MN.decode_cores(data["first_input"]), MN.decode_cores(data["second_input"])
    vectors(key) = MN.parse_fraction.(data[key])
    proof=(;
        cores = MN.decode_cores(data["output"]),
        bridges = [
            reshape(MN.parse_fraction.(R["entries"]), Int.(R["dimensions"])...) for
            R in data["bridges"]
        ],
        residual_bounds = vectors("residual_bounds"),
        prefix_bounds = vectors("prefix_bounds"),
        operator_bounds = vectors("operator_bounds"),
        hs_bounds = vectors("hs_bounds"),
        weights = isnothing(data["weights"]) ? nothing : vectors("weights"),
        first_gauges = isnothing(data["first_gauges"]) ? nothing :
                       MN.decode_gauges(data["first_gauges"]),
        error = MN.parse_fraction(data["error"]),
    )
    return A, B, proof
end

end

"""
    ThermalMPOGap.CertifiedMPO.AdjointTrace

Conditional trace enclosure for a sequence of approximate Hermitian squares or reflected
Gram steps (`trace_interval`). Moved verbatim from spin2 `Spin2AdjointTrace`.
"""
module AdjointTrace

using ..CertifiedMPO: F

"""
Conditional trace enclosure for a sequence of approximate Hermitian squares.

Let A[j+1]=A[j]^2/kappa[j], with Hermitian A and B, and G[end]=B[end].
Define R[j]=B[j]^2/kappa[j]-B[j+1] and
T[j]=(B[j]*G[j+1]+G[j+1]*B[j])/kappa[j]-G[j], with Hermitian G.
The signed center is
  norm(B[end],HS)^2 + 2inner(G[1],A[1]-B[1]) + 2sum(inner(G[j+1],R[j])).
Inputs enclose this center and bound the HS primal errors, HS dual defects,
and operator norms of G[j+1]. All these inputs require separate certification.

Telescoping gives an uncertain remainder bounded by
  2sum(tau[j]*epsilon[j]+gamma[j]*epsilon[j]^2/kappa[j]),
plus the nonnegative terminal squared error, at most epsilon[end]^2.

The same scalar enclosure applies to non-Hermitian candidates and reflected
Gram steps F_j(A)=S_j(A'*A)/kappa[j], where S_j is identity or a self-adjoint
unitary spatial reflection. Use the real HS inner product and replace R[j]
by F_j(B[j])-B[j+1] and T[j] by
  B[j]*(S_j(G[j+1])+S_j(G[j+1])')/kappa[j]-G[j].
The nonlinear remainder is S_j(D[j]'*D[j])/kappa[j]; its pairing with
G[j+1] has absolute value at most norm(G[j+1],op)*norm(D[j],HS)^2/kappa[j].
"""
function trace_interval(
    center_lower::F,
    center_upper::F;
    errors,
    dual_defects,
    dual_operator_bounds,
    normalizations,
    initial_uncertainty = F(0),
)
    steps = length(normalizations)
    @assert length(errors) == steps+1
    @assert length(dual_defects) == length(dual_operator_bounds) == steps
    @assert center_lower <= center_upper && initial_uncertainty >= 0
    @assert all(>=(0), errors) && all(>=(0), dual_defects) && all(>=(0), dual_operator_bounds)
    @assert all(>(0), normalizations)
    cross = 2sum(dual_defects[j]*errors[j] for j in 1:steps; init = F(0))
    quadratic =
        2sum(dual_operator_bounds[j]*errors[j]^2/normalizations[j] for j in 1:steps; init = F(0))
    radius = initial_uncertainty+cross+quadratic
    return (;
        lower = center_lower-radius,
        upper = center_upper+radius+last(errors)^2,
        cross,
        quadratic,
        terminal = last(errors)^2,
        radius,
    )
end

end

# The exact-constant doubling recurrence (Theorem 2.4) and its scalar constants (§2.6).
#
# Seed pair (s, t) = (εₛ, εₜ). One doubling step is the map R(s, t) = (s', t') with
#     z₁ = z(s, t),  s' = f(z₁),  z₂ = z(t, s'),  t' = f(z₂),
#     z(a, b) = 1 - (1 - b)(1 - a)²,   f(z) = z² / (2(1 - z)²).
# At scale j the thermal purity of every even L ∈ [n_j, 2n_j] is at least 1 - z_j, where
# z_j = z(s_j, t_j), so Δ_L ≥ b_j = log((1 - z_j)/z_j) / β_j whenever z_j < 1/2.

export squaring_defect, zdefect, doubling_map, doubling_orbit, gap_rates, gap_bound,
    diagonal_defect, diagonal_fixed_point, fixed_point_bracket_holds, majorant_loss

"Squaring bound f(z) = z²/(2(1-z)²): the defect after squaring a spectrum of defect z."
squaring_defect(z) = z^2 / (2 * (1 - z)^2)

"""
    diagonal_defect(ε) = ((1−ε)^{−3} − 1)² / 2

First component of one doubling step from the diagonal seed (ε, ε). Its fixed point is ε⋆
(`diagonal_fixed_point`); the scope note writes it δ(ε).
"""
diagonal_defect(ε) = squaring_defect(1 - (1 - ε)^3)

"z(a, b) = 1 - (1-b)(1-a)², written without cancellation."
zdefect(a, b) = -expm1(log1p(-b) + 2 * log1p(-a))

"One step of the exact recurrence; `nothing` when an argument of f leaves [0, 2-√2)."
function doubling_map(s, t)
    zstar = 2 - sqrt(oftype(float(s), 2))
    z1 = zdefect(s, t)
    z1 < zstar || return nothing
    s′ = squaring_defect(z1)
    z2 = zdefect(t, s′)
    z2 < zstar || return nothing
    return (s′, squaring_defect(z2))
end

"""
    doubling_orbit(s, t; steps = 60)

Orbit `[(s₀,t₀), (s₁,t₁), …]` of the exact map, in the number type of `s` and `t`.
Use `BigFloat` for more than a handful of steps: the defects fall doubly exponentially.
Returns `nothing` if the orbit leaves the domain of the map.
"""
function doubling_orbit(s, t; steps = 60)
    orbit = [(s, t)]
    for _ in 1:steps
        next = doubling_map(orbit[end]...)
        next === nothing && return nothing
        push!(orbit, next)
    end
    return orbit
end

"Per-scale rates b_j = log((1-z_j)/z_j)/β_j along an orbit (−Inf when z_j ≥ 1/2)."
function gap_rates(orbit, β₀)
    map(enumerate(orbit)) do (j, (s, t))
        z = zdefect(s, t)
        z < 1 // 2 ? log((1 - z) / z) / (β₀ * 2^(j - 1)) : oftype(z, -Inf)
    end
end

"""
    gap_bound(εₛ, εₜ, β₀; steps = 60, precision = 4096)

Uniform gap bound min_j b_j from seed defects, in `BigFloat` arithmetic (not outward rounded;
see `certified_gap_bound` for the rigorous version). For seeds in the admissible region the
rates are nonincreasing (Theorem 2.20), so this returns b_steps, which exceeds the limit b_∞ by at
most 2^{-steps} log 5 / β₀ once r_steps ≤ 1/10 (Lemma 2.21(ii)).
"""
function gap_bound(εₛ, εₜ, β₀; steps = 60, precision = 4096)
    setprecision(BigFloat, precision) do
        orbit = doubling_orbit(BigFloat(εₛ), BigFloat(εₜ); steps)
        orbit === nothing && return nothing
        Float64(minimum(gap_rates(orbit, BigFloat(β₀))))
    end
end

"""
    diagonal_fixed_point(; precision = 256)

The diagonal threshold ε⋆ (Theorem 2.17): the positive root of (1-ε)^{-3} = 1 + √(2ε),
found by bisection. Diagonal seeds ε < ε⋆ contract to zero; seeds ≥ (ε⋆, ε⋆) do not.
"""
function diagonal_fixed_point(; precision = 256)
    setprecision(BigFloat, precision) do
        G(ε) = ((1 - ε)^-3 - 1)^2 - 2ε
        lo, hi = BigFloat("0.1"), BigFloat("0.2")
        for _ in 1:precision
            mid = (lo + hi) / 2
            G(mid) < 0 ? (lo = mid) : (hi = mid)
        end
        (lo + hi) / 2
    end
end

"Exact rational check of the bracket 0.12731 < ε⋆ < 0.12732: G changes sign on it."
function fixed_point_bracket_holds(lo = 12731 // 100000, hi = 12732 // 100000)
    G(ε) = ((1 - ε)^-3 - 1)^2 - 2ε
    G(big(lo)) < 0 < G(big(hi))
end

"""
    majorant_loss(R₀, P₀; J = 40)

The majorant recursion Φ of Lemma 2.21(i), started at (R₀, P₀) ≥ (r₀, ρ₀). Returns
`(Λ_J, tail_ok)`, where Λ_J bounds the loss Λ in β₀ b_∞ = log(1/r₀) − Λ, and `tail_ok` is the
hypothesis Φ(R_{J-1}, P_{J-1}) ≤ (R_{J-1}, P_{J-1}) under which the bound is valid.
Works for any number type that supports the arithmetic, including intervals.
"""
function majorant_loss(R₀, P₀; J = 40)
    function Φ(R, P)
        U = R * (2P + R / 2)
        Q = (2P + R / 2)^2 / (2 * (1 - U)^2)
        T = Q * R^2
        η = (1 + Q) / (1 - R^2 - T) - 1
        P′ = min(one(P), Q / ((1 - R^2 / 4) + Q * (1 - R^2 / 2)^2))
        return R^2 * (1 + η), P′, η
    end
    R, P = R₀, P₀
    Λ = zero(R₀)
    η = zero(R₀)
    Rprev, Pprev = R, P
    for j in 0:(J - 1)
        Rprev, Pprev = R, P
        R, P, η = Φ(R, P)
        Λ += log(1 + η) / 2^(j + 1)
    end
    Λ += log(1 + η) / 2^J
    # Tail hypothesis: Φ(R_{J-1}, P_{J-1}) = (R_J, P_J) ≤ (R_{J-1}, P_{J-1}).
    tail_ok = _le(R, Rprev) && _le(P, Pprev)
    return Λ, tail_ok
end

_le(a::Real, b::Real) = a <= b
_le(a::Interval, b::Interval) = sup(a) <= inf(b)

"""
    ThermalMPOGap.CertifiedMPO.GaugeSearch

Numerical gauge proposals only: Schmidt-balanced full-matrix gauges and a log-diagonal gauge
descent. Every proposal still needs a rational witness from `Norms`. Moved verbatim from
spin2 `Spin2MPOGaugeSearch`; `MN` is `CertifiedMPO.Norms`.
"""
module GaugeSearch

using LinearAlgebra
import ..Norms
const MN = Norms
export gauge_objective, optimize_gauge

import ..ChargeBlocks

"Numerical full-matrix gauges balancing left Schmidt scales against right-canonical tails."
function schmidt_gauge_proposal(cores; floor_ratio = 1e-18, physical_charges = nothing)
    if !isnothing(physical_charges)
        return ChargeBlocks.schmidt_gauges(
            cores,
            physical_charges;
            floor_ratio,
            svd_function = MN.numerical_svd,
        )
    end
    @assert 0 < floor_ratio < 1
    gauges = [ones(1, 1)]
    prefix = ones(1, 1)
    for core in cores[1:(end-1)]
        l, d, di, r = size(core)
        contracted = prefix*reshape(core, l, d*di*r)
        columns = reshape(contracted, size(prefix, 1)*d*di, r)
        prefix = Matrix(qr(columns).R)
        # Near a boundary, the auxiliary rank can exceed the physical prefix
        # dimension. Retain and regularize the full right nullspace as well.
        decomposition = MN.numerical_svd(prefix; full = true)
        singular = vcat(decomposition.S, zeros(r-length(decomposition.S)))
        scales = sqrt.(max.(singular, floor_ratio*first(decomposition.S)))
        push!(gauges, Matrix(Diagonal(scales)*decomposition.Vt))
    end
    push!(gauges, ones(1, 1))
    return gauges
end

"Numerical diagnostic only; rational local norm witnesses are still required."
function matrix_gauge_objective(cores, gauges)
    @assert length(gauges) == length(cores)+1
    value = 0.0
    for (j, core) in enumerate(cores)
        l, d, di, r = size(core)
        left = gauges[j]*reshape(core, l, d*di*r)
        transformed = reshape(reshape(left, l*d*di, r)/gauges[j+1], l, d, di, r)
        value += log(opnorm(MN.local_operator(transformed)))
    end
    return value
end

function gauge_objective(cores, x)
    dimensions = [size(c, 4) for c in cores[1:(end-1)]]
    ends = cumsum(vcat(0, dimensions))
    weights =
        vcat([zeros(1)], [x[(ends[j]+1):ends[j+1]] for j in eachindex(dimensions)], [zeros(1)])
    gradient = [zeros(length(w)) for w in weights]
    value = 0.0
    for (j, core) in enumerate(cores)
        l, d, _, r = size(core)
        transformed =
            core .* reshape(exp.(weights[j]), l, 1, 1, 1) .*
            reshape(exp.(-weights[j+1]), 1, 1, 1, r)
        W = reshape(permutedims(transformed, (2, 4, 3, 1)), d*r, d*l)
        s = MN.numerical_svd(W)
        sigma = first(s.S)
        value += log(sigma)
        cluster = findall(v->v >= sigma*(1-1e-10), s.S)
        for k in cluster
            gradient[j] += vec(sum(reshape(abs2.(s.V[:, k]), d, l); dims = 1))/length(cluster)
            gradient[j+1] -= vec(sum(reshape(abs2.(s.U[:, k]), d, r); dims = 1))/length(cluster)
        end
    end
    return value, vcat(gradient[2:(end-1)]...)
end

function optimize_gauge(cores; iterations = 200)
    x = zeros(sum(size(c, 4) for c in cores[1:(end-1)]))
    value, gradient = gauge_objective(cores, x)
    initial = value
    for iteration in 1:iterations
        norm(gradient, Inf) < 1e-7 && break
        direction = -gradient
        step = 10.0
        candidate = x+step*direction
        trial, gn = gauge_objective(cores, candidate)
        while trial > value-1e-4*step*dot(gradient, gradient) && step > 1e-8
            step /= 2
            candidate = x+step*direction
            trial, gn = gauge_objective(cores, candidate)
        end
        step <= 1e-8 && break
        x, value, gradient = candidate, trial, gn
    end
    return (; initial, final = value, x, gradient_norm = norm(gradient, Inf))
end

end

"""
    ThermalMPOGap.CertifiedMPO.PolynomialBounds

Exact Taylor thermal majorants Q(K) ≥ exp(-δK) with a scalar inflation bound, Arb-accepted
rational upper endpoints, and the positive sum-of-squares form of even Taylor polynomials.
Moved verbatim from spin2 `Spin2PolynomialBounds`, except that the spectral radius of
K = H + nI, hard-coded there as 5n (the spin-2 bond spectrum), is now the keyword `radius`,
whose default `5n` reproduces spin2 exactly.
"""
module PolynomialBounds

import Nemo
using ..CertifiedMPO: F

"Accept a rational upper endpoint by an outward-rounded ball comparison."
function rational_upper(x; bits = 128)
    denominator = big(2)^bits
    center = round(BigInt, BigFloat(x)*BigFloat(denominator))
    radius = big(2)
    RR = parent(x)
    while !(x < RR((center+radius)//denominator))
        radius *= 2
    end
    return (center+radius)//denominator
end

"A rational ball upper endpoint with relative dyadic resolution."
function relative_upper(x; bits = 128)
    value = BigFloat(x)
    exponent2 = iszero(value) ? 0 : exponent(abs(value))
    scale = exponent2 >= 0 ? F(big(2)^exponent2) : F(1, big(2)^(-exponent2))
    return scale*rational_upper(x/parent(x)(scale); bits)
end

"""
Exact polynomial thermal majorant, requiring no Trotter formula.

For K=H+nI, the spin-2 bond spectrum gives -5n I <= K <= 5n I.
Other models pass their own radius M with -M I <= K <= M I (default M = 5n).
Let delta=beta/(2m), m=2^power, and choose rational
r >= exp(delta*M)*(delta*M)^3/6. Then
Q=I-delta*K+delta^2*K^2/2+r*I >= exp(-delta*K)>0.
Both are functions of K, so eigenvalue comparison gives
Z_H(beta) <= exp(beta*n)*Tr(Q^(2m)).

The scalar inflation bound compares this EXACT polynomial trace with Z.
It does not certify an MPO approximation or contraction of that trace.
"""
function seed(n, beta, power; precision = 192, radius = 5n)
    @assert n isa Integer && power isa Integer
    @assert iseven(n) && n >= 4 && beta > 0 && power >= 0
    @assert beta isa Union{Integer,Rational}
    RR = Nemo.ArbField(precision)
    m = big(2)^power
    delta = F(beta)/(2m)
    M = radius
    x = RR(delta*M)
    remainder = rational_upper(exp(x)*x^3/6)
    # |Q-e^{-delta K}| <= 2r, and e^{-delta K} >= e^{-delta M}I.
    # Thus Q^(2m) <= (1+2r e^{delta M})^(2m) e^{-beta K}.
    # 1+y <= e^y supplies the recorded simpler scalar bound.
    log_inflation = 4m*RR(remainder)*exp(x)
    inflation_upper = rational_upper(exp(log_inflation))
    return (;
        n,
        beta = F(beta),
        m,
        power,
        delta,
        spectral_radius = M,
        remainder,
        identity = F(1)+remainder,
        linear = -delta,
        quadratic = delta^2/2,
        inflation_upper,
        log_inflation,
        precision,
    )
end

polynomial(c, x) = c.identity+c.linear*x+c.quadratic*x^2

"""
Higher-order Taylor majorant with the same spectral comparison as `seed`.

For degree d and x=delta*radius (default radius 5n), choose r >= exp(x)*x^(d+1)/(d+1)!.
Then Q(K)=sum((-delta*K)^k/k!, k=0:d)+r*I >= exp(-delta*K)>0.
The scalar log-inflation is at most 4m*r*exp(x). This certifies only
the exact polynomial; a compressed MPO still needs its own error witness.
The existing quadratic seed and its saved witnesses are unchanged.
"""
function taylor_seed(n, beta, power, degree; precision = 192, radius = 5n)
    @assert n isa Integer && power isa Integer && degree isa Integer
    @assert iseven(n) && n >= 4 && beta > 0 && power >= 0 && degree >= 1
    @assert beta isa Union{Integer,Rational}
    RR = Nemo.ArbField(precision)
    m = big(2)^power
    delta = F(beta)/(2m)
    x = RR(delta*radius)
    remainder = relative_upper(exp(x)*x^(degree+1)/factorial(big(degree+1)))
    coefficients = F[F(1)+remainder]
    coefficient = F(1)
    for k in 1:degree
        coefficient *= -delta/k
        push!(coefficients, coefficient)
    end
    log_inflation_upper = relative_upper(4m*RR(remainder)*exp(x))
    operator_upper = sum(abs(coefficients[k+1])*big(radius)^k for k in 0:degree)
    return (;
        n,
        beta = F(beta),
        power,
        degree,
        m,
        delta,
        spectral_radius = radius,
        remainder,
        coefficients,
        operator_upper,
        log_inflation_upper,
        precision,
    )
end

function taylor_polynomial(c, x)
    value = last(c.coefficients)
    for coefficient in Iterators.reverse(c.coefficients[1:(end-1)])
        value = value*x+coefficient
    end
    return value
end

"""
Exact positive sum of squares for the even Taylor polynomial P_(2k)(x).

P_(2k)(x) = integral_0^infinity exp(-t)*(t+x)^(2k) dt / (2k)!.
The moment Gram matrix of (t+x)^k is positive definite. Rational LDL'
therefore expresses P_(2k) as positive rational weights times squares of
degree-k polynomials. Coefficient equality is checked exactly below.
"""
function even_taylor_sos(degree)
    @assert degree isa Integer && degree >= 2 && iseven(degree)
    k = div(degree, 2)
    G = [
        F(binomial(big(k), i)*binomial(big(k), j)*factorial(big(2k-i-j)), factorial(big(2k)))
        for i in 0:k, j in 0:k
    ]
    L, weights = zeros(F, k+1, k+1), zeros(F, k+1)
    for j in 1:(k+1)
        L[j, j] = 1
        weights[j] = G[j, j]-sum((L[j, h]^2*weights[h] for h in 1:(j-1)); init = F(0))
        @assert weights[j] > 0
        for i in (j+1):(k+1)
            L[i, j] =
                (G[i, j]-sum((L[i, h]*L[j, h]*weights[h] for h in 1:(j-1)); init = F(0)))/weights[j]
        end
    end
    polynomials = [L[:, j] for j in 1:(k+1)]
    coefficients = zeros(F, degree+1)
    for (weight, polynomial) in zip(weights, polynomials), i in 0:k, j in 0:k
        coefficients[i+j+1] += weight*polynomial[i+1]*polynomial[j+1]
    end
    @assert coefficients == [F(1, factorial(big(j))) for j in 0:degree]
    return (; weights, polynomials)
end

end
"""
    ThermalMPOGap.CertifiedMPO.MPOAlgebra

Exact rational MPO algebra: direct sums, local products, exact right-tail compression with
rational intertwiners and its replay, invertible conditioning gauges, the certified initial
HS error between two MPOs, and sparse expansion for small controls.

Moved verbatim from the d-generic part of spin2 `Spin2PolynomialMPO`. Where spin2 hard-coded
the spin-2 local dimension 5 or the weights `WEIGHTS = [1, 4, 6, 4, 1]`, the functions take
`d` or `weights` keywords whose defaults reproduce spin2 exactly:

* `identity_mpo(n; d = 5)`;
* `linear_combination(mpos, coefficients; d = size(first(first(mpos)), 2))` (spin2 always
  passed d = 5 cores, and any other d failed there);
* `condition_right_exact(cores; weights = WEIGHTS, …)` and
  `initial_error(exact, candidate; weights = WEIGHTS, …)`.
"""
module MPOAlgebra

using LinearAlgebra, SparseArrays
import Nemo
using ..CertifiedMPO: nemo_array
import ..Norms, ..Squaring, ..PolynomialBounds
const MS = Squaring
const MN = Norms
const PG = PolynomialBounds
const F = MN.F

"Binomial physical weights of spin2's polynomial basis (S = 2); the default `weights`."
const WEIGHTS = F[1, 4, 6, 4, 1]

identity_mpo(n; d = 5) = fill(reshape(Matrix{F}(I, d, d), 1, d, d, 1), n)

"Exact direct sum of MPOs; coefficients enter only the first core."
function linear_combination(mpos, coefficients; d = size(first(first(mpos)), 2))
    n = length(first(mpos))
    @assert n >= 2 && length(mpos) == length(coefficients)
    @assert all(length(m)==n for m in mpos)
    result = Array{F,4}[]
    cache = Dict{Tuple,Array{F,4}}()
    for j in 1:n
        key = (j==1, j==n, Tuple(objectid(m[j]) for m in mpos))
        if haskey(cache, key)
            push!(result, cache[key])
            continue
        end
        left = j==1 ? 1 : sum(size(m[j], 1) for m in mpos)
        right = j==n ? 1 : sum(size(m[j], 4) for m in mpos)
        core = zeros(F, left, d, d, right)
        lo, ro = 0, 0
        for (m, c) in zip(mpos, coefficients)
            l, _, _, r = size(m[j])
            lr, rr = (j==1 ? (1:1) : ((lo+1):(lo+l))), (j==n ? (1:1) : ((ro+1):(ro+r)))
            core[lr, :, :, rr] += (j==1 ? c : F(1))*m[j]
            lo += l
            ro += r
        end
        cache[key] = core
        push!(result, core)
    end
    return result
end

"Exact local multiplication, exploiting sparse nonzero auxiliary blocks."
function product_core(A, B)
    la, d, mid, ra = size(A)
    lb, mid2, di, rb = size(B)
    @assert mid == mid2
    C = zeros(F, la*lb, d, di, ra*rb)
    blocks(X) =
        [(l, r, X[l, :, :, r]) for l in axes(X, 1), r in axes(X, 4) if any(!iszero, X[l, :, :, r])]
    for (l1, r1, a) in blocks(A), (l2, r2, b) in blocks(B)
        C[l1+la*(l2-1), :, :, r1+ra*(r2-1)] += a*b
    end
    return C
end

function product_mpo(A, B)
    @assert length(A) == length(B)
    cache = Dict{Tuple{UInt,UInt},Array{F,4}}()
    return [get!(cache, (objectid(a), objectid(b))) do
        product_core(a, b)
    end for (a, b) in zip(A, B)]
end

"Remove exact right-tail linear dependencies, with rational local intertwiners."
function exact_compress_right(cores)
    n = length(cores)
    @assert n >= 2
    compressed = copy(cores)
    transforms = [zeros(F, 0, 0) for _ in 1:(n+1)]
    transforms[1] = transforms[end] = ones(F, 1, 1)
    for j in n:-1:2
        l, d, di, r = size(compressed[j])
        M = Nemo.matrix(Nemo.QQ, reshape(compressed[j], l, d*di*r))
        rank, reduced = Nemo.rref(M)
        @assert rank > 0
        basis = reduced[1:rank, 1:Nemo.ncols(M)]
        pivots = [findfirst(k -> !iszero(basis[i, k]), 1:Nemo.ncols(M)) for i in 1:rank]
        L = M[1:l, pivots]
        @assert M == L*basis
        transforms[j] = nemo_array(L)
        compressed[j] = reshape(nemo_array(basis), rank, d, di, r)
        lp, dp, dip, rp = size(compressed[j-1])
        @assert rp == l
        previous = Nemo.matrix(Nemo.QQ, reshape(compressed[j-1], lp*dp*dip, rp))*L
        compressed[j-1] = reshape(nemo_array(previous), lp, dp, dip, rank)
    end
    @assert verify_exact_compression(cores, compressed, transforms)
    return (; cores = compressed, transforms)
end

"Check local intertwining identities; they telescope to exact MPO equality."
function verify_exact_compression(original, compressed, transforms)
    n = length(original)
    @assert length(compressed) == n && length(transforms) == n+1
    @assert transforms[1] == transforms[end] == ones(F, 1, 1)
    for j in 1:n
        l, d, di, r = size(original[j])
        lc, dc, dic, rc = size(compressed[j])
        @assert (d, di) == (dc, dic)
        @assert size(transforms[j]) == (l, lc) && size(transforms[j+1]) == (r, rc)
        rhs =
            Nemo.matrix(Nemo.QQ, transforms[j]) *
            Nemo.matrix(Nemo.QQ, reshape(compressed[j], lc, d*di*rc))
        lhs_flat =
            Nemo.matrix(Nemo.QQ, reshape(original[j], l*d*di, r)) *
            Nemo.matrix(Nemo.QQ, transforms[j+1])
        for a in 1:rc, t in 1:di, s in 1:d, b in 1:l
            @assert lhs_flat[b+l*(s-1)+l*d*(t-1), a] == rhs[b, s+d*(t-1)+d*di*(a-1)]
        end
    end
    return true
end

encode_transforms(transforms) =
    [Dict("dimensions"=>collect(size(T)), "entries"=>string.(vec(T))) for T in transforms]

decode_transforms(encoded) =
    [reshape(MN.parse_fraction.(T["entries"]), Int.(T["dimensions"])...) for T in encoded]

"Condition right-tail bases by invertible rational gauges, preserving exact equality."
function condition_right_exact(cores; precision = 256, bits = 80, weights = WEIGHTS)
    result = copy(cores)
    transforms = [ones(F, 1, 1) for _ in 1:(length(cores)+1)]
    for j in length(cores):-1:2
        l, d, di, r = size(result[j])
        M = reshape(result[j], l, d*di*r)
        metric = repeat(vec([F(weights[t])/F(weights[s]) for s in 1:d, t in 1:di]), r)
        gram, _ = MN.weighted_gram(Matrix(transpose(M)); row_metric = metric, precision)
        @assert size(M, 2) >= l
        L = Nemo.cholesky(gram)
        T = setprecision(BigFloat, precision) do
            proposed = [i>=k ? BigFloat(L[i, k]) : BigFloat(0) for i in 1:l, k in 1:l]
            rounded = MS.relative_quantize(proposed; bits)
            for k in 1:l
                if iszero(rounded[k, k])
                    rounded[k, k] = only(MS.relative_quantize([proposed[k, k]]; bits))
                end
            end
            rounded
        end
        @assert all(!iszero(T[k, k]) for k in 1:l)
        exactT = Nemo.matrix(Nemo.QQ, T)
        exactM = Nemo.matrix(Nemo.QQ, M)
        C = Nemo.solve(exactT, exactM; side = :right)
        @assert exactT*C == exactM
        result[j] = reshape(nemo_array(C), l, d, di, r)
        previous = result[j-1]
        lp, dp, dip, rp = size(previous)
        @assert rp == l
        result[j-1] = reshape(
            nemo_array(Nemo.matrix(Nemo.QQ, reshape(previous, lp*dp*dip, rp))*exactT),
            lp,
            dp,
            dip,
            l,
        )
        transforms[j] = T
    end
    @assert verify_exact_compression(cores, result, transforms)
    return (; cores = result, transforms)
end

"Certified initial error from three ordinary double-layer contractions."
function initial_error(exact, candidate; precision = 192, weights = WEIGHTS)
    qq = MS.hs_inner_ball(exact, exact; weights, precision)
    cc = MS.hs_inner_ball(candidate, candidate; weights, precision)
    qc = MS.hs_inner_ball(exact, candidate; weights, precision)
    error2 = qq+cc-2qc
    upper2 = max(F(0), PG.relative_upper(error2))
    error = MN.relative_upper_sqrt(upper2)
    @assert error2 < parent(error2)(error^2)
    return (; error, qq, cc, qc, error2)
end

"Exact sparse physical expansion for independent small-system controls."
function sparse_operator(cores)
    partial = [sparse(ones(F, 1, 1))]
    for core in cores
        l, d, _, r = size(core)
        next = [spzeros(F, d*size(first(partial), 1), d*size(first(partial), 2)) for _ in 1:r]
        for a in 1:r, b in 1:l
            C = sparse(core[b, :, :, a])
            (iszero(nnz(C)) || iszero(nnz(partial[b]))) && continue
            next[a] += kron(partial[b], C)
        end
        partial = next
    end
    return only(partial)
end

end

"""
    ThermalMPOGap.Results

Writing results and recording where they came from: atomic JSON output, SHA-256 fingerprints
of source trees and environments, run metadata, and JSON parsing that never routes a large
integer through `Float64`.
"""
module Results

using Dates, JSON3, LinearAlgebra, SHA

export write_result, sha256_file, file_hashes, source_hashes, run_metadata,
    parse_exact_json, read_exact_json

"""
    write_result(path, data) -> path

Write `data` as pretty JSON with a trailing newline, atomically: a crash leaves either the old
file or the new one, never a partial file.
"""
function write_result(path, data)
    mkpath(dirname(abspath(path)))
    temporary = path * ".tmp"
    open(temporary, "w") do io
        JSON3.pretty(io, data)
        println(io)
    end
    mv(temporary, path; force = true)
    return path
end

"Hex SHA-256 of a file's bytes."
sha256_file(path) = bytes2hex(sha256(read(path)))

"""
    file_hashes(root, names; prefix = "") -> Dict

SHA-256 of each `root/name`, keyed by `prefix * name`.
"""
file_hashes(root, names; prefix = "") =
    Dict(prefix * name => sha256_file(joinpath(root, name)) for name in names)

"""
    source_hashes(root; dirs = ("src", "scripts", "test"), files = (), skip_missing = true)

SHA-256 of every `.jl` file under `root/dir` for each `dir`, plus the listed `files`, keyed by
path relative to `root`. Missing directories are skipped unless `skip_missing = false`.
"""
function source_hashes(root; dirs = ("src", "scripts", "test"), files = (),
    skip_missing = true)
    paths = String[joinpath(root, name) for name in files]
    for dir in dirs
        top = joinpath(root, dir)
        isdir(top) || (skip_missing ? continue : error("missing source directory $top"))
        for (folder, _, names) in walkdir(top), name in names
            endswith(name, ".jl") && push!(paths, joinpath(folder, name))
        end
    end
    return Dict(relpath(path, root) => sha256_file(path) for path in sort(paths))
end

"""
    run_metadata(config; source_sha256, packages = (), status, certified = false)

The provenance record stored with a numerical result: creation time, Julia version, the
version of each package module in `packages`, thread counts, the run configuration and the
source fingerprint.
"""
function run_metadata(config; source_sha256, packages = (), status, certified = false)
    record = Dict{String,Any}(
        "created_utc" => string(now(UTC)),
        "julia" => string(VERSION),
        "julia_threads" => Threads.nthreads(),
        "blas_threads" => BLAS.get_num_threads(),
        "config" => config,
        "source_sha256" => source_sha256,
        "certified" => certified,
        "status" => status,
    )
    for package in packages
        record[string(nameof(package))] = string(pkgversion(package))
    end
    return record
end

"Parse JSON with every bare integer token read as a string, so big integers stay exact."
function parse_exact_json(raw::AbstractString)
    tokens = r"\"(?:\\.|[^\"\\])*\"|-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?"
    exact =
        replace(raw, tokens => s -> startswith(s, '"') || occursin(r"[.eE]", s) ? s : '"' * s * '"')
    return JSON3.read(exact, Any)
end

"`parse_exact_json` of a file."
read_exact_json(path) = parse_exact_json(read(path, String))
